messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Node node-az1-gpu-12 reported CUDA OOM during inference (model: gpt-medium-q4). headroom reported: 4.8GB. auto-evict: false. Instances affected: 3/48 replicas. Runbook: <https://runbooks.redwood.local/gpu-oom|gpu-oom>
sre-oncall: ack — looking now. Paging @infra-eng and @ml-runtime. Anyone on-call for this pool? :loud_sound:
infra-eng: on it, grabbing dmesg and runtime logs. quick question: is this the pool with sparepool_reserve enabled? If reserved blocks pinned, headroom is misleading.
ml-runtime: pulling runtime telemetry. KV-cache growth spiked right before OOM. snippet:

```text
[2026-03-15T12:02:03Z] alloc_try: requested 1.2G, available headroom 4.8G
[2026-03-15T12:02:03Z] cudalloc failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
reserved_blocks: 42, spare_pool_free: 1, fragmentation_ratio: 0.72
runtime_flags: --kv-cache=enabled --reserved-block-target=64
```
alice: fwiw we hit a similar pattern yesterday on az2 — reserved blocks were pinned and fragmentation >0.7. headroom counted free slabs that were unusable due to pinned reserves. We can try soft-evict first to avoid dropping live requests.
infra-eng: agreed. prefer runtime soft-evict to avoid container churn. issuing soft-evict for KV cache on node-az1-gpu-12 now.
infra-eng: running:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood.local/admin/evict" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${INTERNAL_TOKEN}" -d '{"node":"node-az1-gpu-12","type":"kv"}'
```
incident-bot: Evict job queued (job_id: evict-2387654321-1). progress: 0%.
ml-runtime: monitoring: spare_pool_free -> 2 after evict, reserved_blocks -> 39. Still seeing sporadic allocation failures. fragmentation_ratio still ~0.69. Soft-evict reduced pressure but not enough for large contiguous allocs.
sre-oncall: we need to reclaim slabs. plan: roll a single replica on the node to trigger slab reclamation, keep min capacity. @infra-eng proceed with r-03 first.
infra-eng: initiating rolling restart of r-03 on node-az1-gpu-12. Command:

```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/r-03 -n serving-pool-az1
```
incident-bot: Deploy job started (job_id: restart-r03-2387654321). Watching healthchecks.
infra-eng: r-03 restarted, container terminated due to OOM on shutdown but came back up. KV cache trimmed on startup. reserved_blocks -> 28, spare_pool_free -> 6.
ml-runtime: post-restart telemetry looks better. allocation attempts succeeding. fragmentation_ratio dropped to 0.52. No new OOMs on that node in the last 90s.
customer-success: FYI, acme-corp reported elevated 504s at 12:04 UTC on two endpoints for ~45s. We messaged them and opened ticket CUST-1129. They escalated to SLO-owner.
alice: mitigation checklist: 1) soft-evict 2) restart one replica 3) lower reserved_block_target for pool and roll config 4) add telemetry for reserved_blocks by model and pinned owner.
ml-runtime: proposing immediate config change (staged): `--reserved-block-target=48 --max-prefetch=64` for az1 pool. Will run preflight then roll. This should reduce pinned blocks and lower prefetch memory pressure.
infra-eng: preflight ok on canary. scheduling stage roll with 5m pacing.
sre-oncall: current impact: limited to 3 replicas on node-az1-gpu-12, degraded latency for a small subset of traffic. Marking Sev2 for now. Mitigations applied (soft-evict + rolling restart + config roll in progress). Monitoring closely.
bob: taking handoff at 12:20 UTC. I'll coordinate overnight window to fully drain and repro root cause. Please post any remaining logs/IDs. I'll follow up with infra to schedule targeted node drain during low traffic.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2387654321. Link: https://incidents.redwood.local/INC-2387654321
alice: follow-up action items: - Add telemetry for per-model reserved_block_count (owner: ml-runtime) - Investigate allocator's coalescing behavior when reserved blocks are pinned (owner: infra-eng) - Consider spare_pool sizing change for high-fragmentation workloads (owner: product/serving)
ml-runtime: noted. I'll add a short eval to trigger high fragmentation scenarios and test eviction paths.
sre-oncall: closing this Slack thread for live mitigation. We'll update the incident doc with timeline and customer impact. If OOMs recur, reopen and escalate to P0.
bob: thanks everyone — I'll post a short postmortem draft tomorrow after root cause triage. :thumbsup:
summary: Soft-evict + rolling restart mitigated CUDA OOM on node-az1-gpu-12 caused by pinned reserved blocks and fragmentation; limited customer impact reported; follow-ups assigned.
